I don't consider it social media, because the way Voat (and Reddit) functions is closer to an oldschool forum than it is to Facebook, Twitter, etc. Users follow and post to groups (subverses) dedicated to a particular subject, that are moderated to varying extents to keep things on-topic. It's easy for a lurking outsider to read a thread here and follow what's going on, because the main focus of the site is group discussion rather than individual streams of thought.

Social media, on the other hand, is based on following individual users and reading everything they have to post about anything. Often, group discussions are difficult to have and even more difficult to follow without being an active participant in them. (I'm looking at you, Twitter and Tumblr!) This is usually due to the site's structure as well as the severe lack of janitorial moderation. Social media is set up for individuals to produce blurbs, not to have bunch of users coming together to have a coherent conversation.
